title: Application control feature configuration and monitoring
content:
## Overview

For each filter in the application control profile, you must indicate an action — what FortiGate does when traffic matches. The available actions are:

- **Allow**: passes the traffic and does not generate a log.
- **Monitor**: passes the traffic, but also generates a log message.
- **Block**: drops the detected traffic and generates a log message.
- **Quarantine**: blocks the traffic from the suspected source until the expiration time is reached, and generates a log message.

If you are not sure which action to choose, **Monitor** can be useful initially while you study your network. After you have studied your network traffic, you can fine-tune your filter selection by choosing the most appropriate action. If an application requires feedback to prevent instability or other unwanted behavior, you might choose Quarantine instead of Block. Otherwise, the most efficient use of FortiGate resources is to block.

![Application control feature configuration and monitoring](diagram:0)

## Additional Options and Block Pages

The application sensor provides additional options:

- **Network Protocol Enforcement**: allows you to configure network services (for example, FTP, HTTP, and HTTPS) on known ports (for example, 21, 80, and 443), while blocking those services on other ports. If a protocol dissector confirms the service of network traffic, Network Protocol Enforcement checks whether the confirmed service is allowlisted under the server port — if not, it is a violation and IPS can take the configured action.
- **Block applications detected on non-default ports**: FortiGate compares the ports used by the application with the ones defined in FortiGuard application signatures. The traffic is blocked if it does not match.
- **Replacement Messages for HTTP-based Applications**: allows you to replace blocked content from HTTP/HTTPS applications with an explanation for the user's benefit. For non-HTTP/HTTPS applications, FortiGate only drops the packets or resets the TCP connection.

For HTTP-based applications, application control can provide a **block page** explaining why the application was blocked. If deep inspection is enabled in the firewall policy, all HTTPS-based applications also provide this block page. The block page contains:

- Signature that detected the application
- Signature category
- URL that was specifically blocked
- User name and group name (if authentication is enabled)
- Universal unique identifier (UUID) of the policy governing the traffic

The UUID helps identify which policy on FortiGate blocked the page, even across a large number of policies and FortiGate devices.

## Scan Order, Priority, and Monitoring

After the IPS engine examines the traffic stream for a signature match, FortiGate scans packets for matches in this order:

1. **Application and filter overrides**: If you have configured application or filter overrides, the application control profile considers those first, starting at the top of the list — like firewall policies.
2. **Categories**: The application control profile then applies the action configured for applications in the selected categories.

The priority in which application and filter overrides are placed takes precedence. For example, if a filter override (such as Excessive-Bandwidth) is placed above an application override, the filter override action applies first — even for applications that are set to Monitor in the overrides section.

After you configure an application control profile, you must apply it to a **firewall policy**. When you enable the logging of security events or all sessions on a firewall policy, application control events are also logged.

You can monitor application control events in:

- **Log & Report > Security Events > Application Control**: shows all application control events with details on source, destination, application, and action.
- **Forward Traffic logs**: also records activity governed by the firewall policy. Use the Policy ID or Policy UUID fields to identify which policy applied application control.
- **Dashboard > FortiView Applications**: shows a summary of traffic matched by application control. Select a specific application to drill down into session and bytes information.

> **Key terms:** Application control can monitor the user's browser history and track web application usage.

> **Key terms:** Dailymotion is blocked because the filter override is checked first and Dailymotion uses excessive bandwidth.
